findings.title: bundleHint assumes the created-branch convention, ignoring the adopted-branch rule documented next to it
findings.detail: bundleHint's only positive branch guess is `"takt/"+slug` (select.go:122-123), and its doc comment states flatly that `takt init` commits the bundle on takt/<slug>. But cmd_init.go's chooseBranch (internal/cli/cmd_init.go:204-206, spec D9) documents two branch outcomes: on the default branch init creates takt/<slug>, but on any other branch init adopts the current branch (bi.adopted=true) and commits the bundle there instead — under whatever name that branch has, not takt/<slug>. For a run initialised via the adopted path, switching away from that branch and running `status`/`unlock` will fail loadBundle with fs.ErrNotExist, bundleHint's BranchExists(ctx, "takt/"+slug) check will correctly return false (no such branch was ever created), and the code falls through to "no run named <slug> under <base>; check the slug or pass --dir" — telling the user no such run exists when it does, just on a differently-named adopted branch. No existing helper maps a slug back to its actual (possibly adopted) branch, so this is a real gap between the new hint logic and the branch rule the surrounding code already knows about, not just an untested edge case.
